from.place: proof step: Noetherian approximation of X, the finitely presented complex, flatness, proper support, and the perfect object (Tags 01ZR, 0C0C, 0A1G, 09RK)

title: Noetherian approximation of the tensor data
statement: Let S=Spec(R) with R a ring written as a filtered colimit of Noetherian rings R_i, and let f:X\to S be of finite presentation [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Let G^\bullet be a bounded complex of finitely presented O_X-modules flat over S with each term having support proper over S [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base], and let E be a perfect object of D(O_X) [def-pc-perfect-complex]. After increasing i, there exist X_i\to Spec(R_i), a bounded complex G_i^\bullet of finitely presented modules flat over R_i with proper support, and a perfect E_i on X_i whose base changes are X, G^\bullet, and E.

source.place: Lemma 32.10.2, Tag 01ZR; Lemma 32.10.4, Tag 05LY; Lemma 32.13.5, Tag 081G, together with Cohomology of Schemes Lemma 30.26.7; Lemma 36.29.3, Tag 09RF

proof.text: Choose a stage in the filtered system at which the finitely presented morphism X\to Spec(R) descends. The spreading-out theorem gives X_i\to Spec(R_i) of finite presentation and an identification of its base change with X.

After increasing the same stage, the bounded complex G^\bullet descends as a bounded complex G_i^\bullet of finitely presented modules, flat over R_i, and the supports of its terms descend with properness over Spec(R_i); the base change is identified with G^\bullet. This is the combined finite-presentation, flatness, and proper-support descent statement.

source.place: Lemmas 32.10.2 (01ZR), 32.10.4 (05LY), 32.13.5 (081G), and Cohomology of Schemes Lemma 30.26.7

proof.text: After increasing the stage once more, the perfect object E descends to a perfect object E_i on X_i with the prescribed base-change identification, by perfect-complex descent along the affine inverse system.

The filtered system is directed, so one stage dominates the stages obtained in the preceding steps. Replacing i by that common later stage and base-changing all descended data preserves finite presentation, boundedness, flatness, proper support, perfectness, and the three stated identifications. Thus all required data descend simultaneously.
